"""ISO 8601 week labels for report partitions."""

from datetime import date, timedelta


def week_one_monday(year: int) -> date:
    """Return the Monday on which ISO week 1 of ``year`` starts."""
    jan1 = date(year, 1, 1)
    return jan1 - timedelta(days=jan1.weekday())


def iso_week_label(d: date) -> str:
    """Return the ISO 8601 week label of ``d`` as ``"YYYY-Www"``.

    Weeks run from Monday to Sunday. Week 1 of a year is the week that
    contains 4 January (equivalently, the week that contains the year's first
    Thursday), and the following weeks are numbered consecutively, so a year
    has 52 or 53 weeks. ``YYYY`` is the ISO week-numbering year, which can
    differ from the calendar year near New Year: a date before the Monday of
    its calendar year's week 1 belongs to the last week of the previous year,
    and a date on or after the Monday of the next year's week 1 belongs to
    week 1 of the next year. The week number is always written with two
    digits, e.g. ``"2025-W07"``.
    """
    year = d.year
    start = week_one_monday(year)
    if d < start:
        year -= 1
        start = week_one_monday(year)
    week = (d - start).days // 7 + 1
    return f"{year}-W{week:02d}"

from datetime import date, timedelta


def week_one_monday(year: int) -> date:
    """Return the Monday on which ISO week 1 of ``year`` starts."""
    jan4 = date(year, 1, 4)
    return jan4 - timedelta(days=jan4.weekday())


def iso_week_label(d: date) -> str:
    """Return the ISO 8601 week label of ``d`` as ``"YYYY-Www"``.

    Weeks run from Monday to Sunday. Week 1 of a year is the week that
    contains 4 January (equivalently, the week that contains the year's first
    Thursday), and the following weeks are numbered consecutively, so a year
    has 52 or 53 weeks. ``YYYY`` is the ISO week-numbering year, which can
    differ from the calendar year near New Year: a date before the Monday of
    its calendar year's week 1 belongs to the last week of the previous year,
    and a date on or after the Monday of the next year's week 1 belongs to
    week 1 of the next year. The week number is always written with two
    digits, e.g. ``"2025-W07"``.
    """
    year = d.year
    start = week_one_monday(year)
    if d < start:
        year -= 1
        start = week_one_monday(year)
    else:
        # Check if d is on or after the Monday of week 1 of the next year
        next_start = week_one_monday(year + 1)
        if d >= next_start:
            year += 1
            start = next_start
    week = (d - start).days // 7 + 1
    return f"{year}-W{week:02d}"

def week_one_monday(year: int) -> date:

    jan4 = date(year, 1, 4)
    # If jan4 is Sunday (weekday 6), we want to go back 6 days to Monday
    # If jan4 is Monday (weekday 0), we want to go back 0 days
    # But for ISO weeks, we need to find the Monday on or before jan4
    # Using (weekday + 1) % 7 to handle Sunday (6) correctly
    offset = (jan4.weekday() + 1) % 7
    if offset == 0:
        offset = 7
    return jan4 - timedelta(days=offset)

12	def iso_week_label(d: date) -> str:
13	    """Return the ISO 8601 week label of ``d`` as ``"YYYY-Www"``.
14	
15	    Weeks run from Monday to Sunday. Week 1 of a year is the week that
16	    contains 4 January (equivalently, the week that contains the year's first
17	    Thursday), and the following weeks are numbered consecutively, so a year
18	    has 52 or 53 weeks. ``YYYY`` is the ISO week-numbering year, which can
19	    differ from the calendar year near New Year: a date before the Monday of
20	    its calendar year's week 1 belongs to the last week of the previous year,
21	    and a date on or after the Monday of the next year's week 1 belongs to
22	    week 1 of the next year. The week number is always written with two
23	    digits, e.g. ``"2025-W07"``.
24	    """
25	    year = d.year
26	    start = week_one_monday(year)
27	    if d < start:
28	        year -= 1
29	        start = week_one_monday(year)
30	    else:
31	        # Check if d is on or after the Monday of week 1 of the next year
32	        next_start = week_one_monday(year + 1)
33	        if d >= next_start:
34	            year += 1
35	            start = next_start
